purpose: Machine-readable inventory of every atomic-ordering, interior-mutability and lock-free publication site, so that AArch64 (weak memory model) exposure is enumerable and drift is detectable. Follows the repository gap-inventory pattern: if something is unverified, it must be enumerable, and a gate must fail closed when the enumeration drifts from the code.

method.static_scan: ripgrep over crates/*/src for Ordering::*, compare_exchange*, fence(, UnsafeCell
method.limits: This is a STATIC inventory only. It does NOT constitute proof of correctness. Loom exhaustive interleaving models and real AArch64 hardware execution are NOT included and remain open work on this bead.
method.host_measured_on: x86-64 (AMD EPYC 7282, 2 NUMA nodes) - no AArch64 hardware was available in this session

key_structural_finding.statement: There is currently NO true lock-free data structure in the repository. Zero UnsafeCell and zero fence() calls exist across all three crates. This is a direct consequence of #![forbid(unsafe_code)]: a classic seqlock requires UnsafeCell and tolerates torn reads, which safe Rust cannot express.
key_structural_finding.consequence: AArch64 weak-memory exposure of EXISTING code is materially lower than a raw Ordering::Relaxed count would suggest. The risk becomes real when BRIDGE-05 introduces the native-code capsule with genuine lock-free code-cache publication.
key_structural_finding.revises: This finding tempers the original framing of this bead. The audit should be understood as establishing the ordering inventory and verification harness BEFORE the capsule lands, rather than as remediating a known existing defect.

sites.relaxed_classification: ALL 23 Relaxed uses are on pure statistics counters (total_reads, fast_path_reads, fallback_reads, total_retries, writer_pressure_observations, retry_budget_fallbacks, uninitialized_fallbacks, writer_pressure_fallbacks, writes). None are on the sequence field or on any correctness-bearing value.
sites.rationale: The sequence field uses exclusively Acquire loads and Release stores, which is textbook seqlock discipline. Critically, the payload is read via self.snapshot_read().clone() under an RwLock read guard, NOT as an unsynchronized raw read. The RwLock supplies its own acquire-on-lock / release-on-unlock ordering for the payload, so the classic seqlock read-side hazard (payload loads sinking past the validating sequence load, which an Acquire load does not prevent) DOES NOT APPLY here. Relaxed on statistics counters is correct and idiomatic.
sites.residual_risk: LOW. This is a seqlock-shaped optimistic-retry wrapper around an RwLock, not a lock-free seqlock. The optimistic sequence check is an additional validity filter layered on an already-synchronized read.
sites.action: Confirm under loom anyway (cheap, and locks in the property before the structure is ever converted to a genuine lock-free form).

sites.rationale: This is the newest concurrent code in the tree (bd-x85a7, landed 2026-07-23) and holds the only compare_exchange in the repository, plus the highest AcqRel density. It governs process-spawn admission and the globally ordered host-effect journal, where ordering is semantically load-bearing for replay identity, not merely for performance.
sites.residual_risk: LOW (revised down from MEDIUM after per-site classification)
sites.action: No ordering change required. Loom modelling of the reserve/complete protocol is still worthwhile, but it would be verifying a Mutex-based protocol for liveness/invariant violations (completion holes, reserve-before-live), NOT for weak-memory reordering. Cross-reference bd-x85a7.1 and bd-x85a7.2.
sites.journal_finding: host_effect_journal.rs contains ZERO atomics. Its state is held in Mutex only (entries: Mutex<Vec<JournalSlot>>, state: Mutex<JournalState>, attempt_entries, attempt_record_start). The global-ordering property the journal claims is therefore enforced by MUTUAL EXCLUSION, not by atomic ordering. A Mutex supplies full acquire-on-lock / release-on-unlock semantics, so the ordering claim holds on any memory model including AArch64. The earlier MEDIUM assessment assumed lock-free publication that does not exist.

per_site_classification.process_spawn.rs:643,653 active_children: CORRECT. Acquire load + compare_exchange_weak(success=AcqRel, failure=Acquire) is the textbook concurrency-limit admission pattern; failure ordering is correctly no stronger than success.
per_site_classification.process_spawn.rs:522,532 active.fetch_su: CORRECT. Permit release on a counting semaphore; AcqRel is conservative and sound.
per_site_classification.process_spawn.rs:1074,1123 active_watchd: CORRECT. Conservative ordering on a liveness counter.
per_site_classification.process_spawn.rs:1652,1761 cancel load(A: CORRECT. Release store paired with Acquire load is the standard cancellation-flag publication idiom; it correctly publishes writes made before the cancel.
per_site_classification.process_spawn.rs:1031 next_handle.fetch_: CORRECT. Unique-ID generation; fetch_add is atomic under any ordering and publishes no other memory.
per_site_classification.process_spawn.rs:590-597 Debug-format lo: CORRECT. Display/diagnostics only; no correctness dependency.

sites.verdict: NOT YET EXISTENT - HIGHEST FUTURE RISK
sites.rationale: The native-code capsule will introduce genuine lock-free publication: concurrent patch/execute/retire on executable memory, epoch invalidation, and retirement-under-read. This is where weak-memory correctness genuinely bites, and where x86-TSO would silently forgive a missing Acquire/Release that AArch64 would not.
sites.action: Loom model the publication/retirement state machine BEFORE the capsule ships, per bead .6.37. This inventory exists so that gate is in place first.

sites.kind: process-unique ID generation for temporary file/directory names
sites.rationale: Every one of these is `COUNTER.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)` used to mint a unique suffix for a temp path, plus two test-only provider call counters in execution_orchestrator.rs. fetch_add is atomic under ANY ordering, so uniqueness -- the only property required -- is guaranteed. Relaxed is correct precisely because the counter publishes no other memory: nothing is read through it, so no happens-before edge is needed. Strengthening these to SeqCst would cost performance and buy nothing.
sites.residual_risk: NONE. Weak memory models do not affect fetch_add atomicity.
sites.action: No change required. Recorded so the classification is complete and drift is detectable.

honest_status: STATIC CLASSIFICATION COMPLETE across all three crates; every atomic-ordering site is classified and correct, and the assessed AArch64 risk for existing code is LOW. This does NOT constitute proof: loom models and real AArch64 hardware execution remain open, and the genuine weak-memory exposure arrives with BRIDGE-05.

relaxed_classification_summary.conclusion: All 46 engine-crate Ordering::Relaxed uses are now individually accounted for and every one is correct. None is on a correctness-bearing publication path. This closes the static-classification portion of the audit and further lowers the assessed AArch64 risk for EXISTING engine code.
relaxed_classification_summary.repository_wide_conclusion: ALL atomic-ordering sites in all three crates are now individually classified and every one is correct. No correctness-bearing Relaxed exists anywhere; the only CAS uses the textbook AcqRel/Acquire pattern; and the one component claiming a global ordering property (host_effect_journal.rs) achieves it via Mutex rather than atomics. Assessed AArch64 risk for ALL EXISTING code is therefore LOW. The genuine weak-memory exposure is entirely prospective and lands with BRIDGE-05 code-cache publication.
